request.system: You are a sceptical results reviewer. Task: rank Medicare providers for audit. Each of 5,410 providers carries a PotentialFraud label (9.35% flagged) whose origin is undocumented; treat it as suspicion, not confirmed fraud. Claims run 27 Nov 2008 to 31 Dec 2009. The primary metric is PR-AUC; the audit queue holds about 100 providers. Pick the configuration to carry forward. Prefer a simpler model unless a more complex one is better by more than one standard deviation of PR-AUC across folds. Flag any result that looks too good. You may request up to 2 more round(s) of experiments; set stop=true if further search is unlikely to help. Rate your confidence in chosen_run (0-1): 1.0 means results are clear-cut and no reasonable reviewer would disagree; 0.5 means the top configs are too close to call or something looks off. (Independent run 1, no feature agent.)

concerns: Run 1 (LightGBM) leads logistic (run 3) by 0.042 PR-AUC, which is less than one fold SD (0.0574 to 0.0677). Under the simplicity rule, logistic regression wins by default.
The fold SDs (~0.06 to 0.075) are large relative to the gaps between all configs, so the ranking is mostly noise. Run 4 and run 1 are statistically indistinguishable, and so are runs 2 and 3.

ROC-AUC is nearly identical across all models (0.942 to 0.943) and PR-AUC differences are small, which suggests a shared strong signal. Logistic matching trees at ROC-AUC ~0.94 hints that a few dominant features, such as volume or size proxies, carry most of the information.

ROC-AUC of 0.94 and precision@50 of ~0.76 are high for fraud labels of unknown origin. The label may be derived from, or correlated with, claim volume or other features (leakage or a proxy label), so the results may reflect how the label was generated rather than actual fraud.
The labels are suspicion, not confirmed fraud. High precision against them may only mean the model reproduces whatever flagging process produced them.
Only 4 configs have been tried, with no repeated seeds. prec@50 is measured on the ~50 top slots per fold, which is noisy, and the audit queue is ~100, so precision at 100 is not reported.

The no_size ablation costs little in ROC-AUC, but its PR-AUC effect is confounded with the model and imbalance changes. Size dependence is unresolved, and size-driven rankings would just surface large providers.
The data span only ~13 months and temporal structure is not described. If folds are not grouped or time-aware, there is leakage risk, and a random split may overstate performance.

next_experiments.rationale: Isolates the effect of removing size features on the simple model with all else equal to run 3. It tests whether the signal is just provider size or volume.
Checks sensitivity of the simple model to regularisation and class weighting. If PR-AUC matches or improves, it confirms the simple baseline is competitive.
A more heavily regularised LightGBM on the same feature set as run 1. It tests whether the tree advantage holds and is stable with lower variance.
